case_name: Ram Kumar Gijroya v Delhi Subordinate Services Selection Board and another

Delhi Subordinate Services Selection Board and another
Supreme Court of India

(C) No. 27551 of 2012) With Civil Appeal No. 1693 of 2016 (Arising Out of S. L. P. (C) No. 309 of 2013) and Civil Appeal No. 1694 of 2016 (Arising Out of S. L. P. (C) No. 21445 of 2013)
(Non-Reportable)
The Judgment was delivered by : V. Gopala Gowda, J.
1. Leave granted.
2. The present appeals arise out of the impugned common judgment and order dated 24.01.2012 passed by the High Court of Delhi in Letters Patent Appeal No.562 of 2011 and Writ Petition (C) No. 8087 of 2011 whereby the High Court set aside the judgment and order dated 24.11.2010 passed in Writ Petition (C) No. 382 of 2009, wherein the learned single Judge had allowed the Writ Petition and directed the respondents to accept the O.B.C. certificate of the appellants herein
facts: The respondent-Delhi Subordinate Services Selection Board (hereinafter referred to as
issues: Whether a candidate who appears in an examination under the O.B.C. category and submits the certificate after the last date mentioned in the advertisement is eligible for selection to the post under the O.B.C. category or not.
petitioner_arguments: The requirement of submitting the O.B.C. certificate before the cut-off date of the application was introduced by the respondent-DSSSB only while declaring the result on 15.12.2008, holding that the appellant was not eligible for selection of the post of Staff Nurse as the O.B.C. certificate was received after cut-off date.
respondent_arguments: The Division Bench of the High Court was justified in not allowing the appellant to submit the O.B.C. certificate after the cut-off date fixed in the advertisement as the appellant had failed to submit the required certificate for availing the benefit of reservation within the stipulated time and thus, he had waived of his right for being considered under the reserved category.
court_reasoning: The Division Bench erred in setting aside the judgment and order passed by the learned single Judge. The Division Bench did not consider the decision rendered in the case of Pushpa 2009 Indlaw DEL 1464 (supra).
holding: We record our reasons hereunder. The Division Bench of the High Court erred in setting aside the judgment and order passed by the learned single Judge.
